architecture.meta.title: XHProf Webman layered architecture
architecture.meta.desc: Three layered diagrams: the top layer is the 11 framework entry classes (4 already supported + 7 new in this release), the middle is the 5 interfaces in src/Core/Contract/, the bottom is the 5 classes in Core. The red band at the bottom marks the only two couplings to frameworks left in Core, and notes that the 7 new frameworks never go through autoDetect — all use explicit injection via Xhprof::bootstrap().

lifecycle.lanes.37: Where each framework starts and stops profiling

lifecycle.meta.title: The lifecycle of one profiled request
lifecycle.meta.desc: The upper half is the 8 stages of a profiled request: request in, the entry class first checking the report page and asset paths (a hit short-circuits without profiling), Xhprof::bootstrap injecting 5 adapters, the isEnabled and extension_loaded double check, xhprofStart, business logic, xhprofStop in finally, and save_run writing to Redis. The lower half is 5 lanes, using coloured bands to mark where PSR-15 (Yii3 / Slim), Symfony, WordPress, Joomla and Drupal each start and stop profiling, plus their shutdown fallbacks.

design.meta.title: Design trade-offs: decision, reason and cost
design.meta.desc: A comparison of five key decisions, each listing the decision, the benefit it bought and the cost it charged: Core depends on 5 contracts only, entry classes serve the report page themselves, no shared layer is extracted, stubs are checked by an independent verification loop, and the six new frameworks use explicit injection rather than autoDetect.
